meta.subtitle: Second-quarter revenue rose 34% and the stock trades at 7.0x forward earnings, but net debt is 4.5x EBITDA and free cash flow repays it slowly

analystCommentary:
Shift4's shares have fallen to $36.31 on October 2, 2026, close to the 52-week low of $34.56 and well under half the high of $80.98. Our data does not say what drove the decline, and we have no news coverage that explains it.

The filing shows a business that is still growing, but one that took on substantial debt to buy Global Blue. Higher interest costs are now absorbing much of the growth before it reaches shareholders, and free cash flow, once reinvestment is counted, is modest against the debt (see Financials).

The valuation is undemanding and the Street's lowest target sits above today's price. Even so, we think the leverage justifies the discount until the company shows it can pay debt down, so we rate the shares HOLD.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Shift4 Payments, Inc. provides software, payment processing, tax-free shopping (TFS) and dynamic currency conversion services. Its technology is used by restaurants, hotels, stadiums, theme parks, luxury retailers and other businesses, from small owner-operated merchants to multinational enterprises. Products include the SkyTab point-of-sale family, the Lighthouse business intelligence suite and an omnichannel payments platform.

The company added a TFS business through its acquisition of Global Blue in the third quarter of 2025. In February 2026 it collapsed its Up-C structure, converting its Founder's and Rook's shares into Class A common stock.

Shift4 was founded in 1999 and is headquartered in Center Valley, Pennsylvania. It distributes through independent software vendors, internal sales and support networks, enterprises and value-added resellers.

thesis.body: The shares trade at 7.0x NTM earnings and a 10.8% trailing FCF yield, a price that implies serious trouble. The filing shows rising volume and revenue, which argues against that. The constraint is the balance sheet: net debt is 4.5x EBITDA, interest coverage is 1.5x, and free cash flow of $400M in FY25 reduces that debt only slowly. Until deleveraging is visible, we see the risk and the reward as roughly balanced.

catalysts: Evidence of debt reduction from free cash flow.
Progress on Global Blue integration and synergies.
A clearer read on how travel disruption is affecting results.
risks: High leverage and thin interest coverage.
A significant Founder stake no longer tied to management.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY25 revenue was $4.2B, up {+25.5%+}, after growth of 29.9% in FY24 and 28.7% in FY23. Operating margin rose from -3.6% in FY21 to 8.4% in FY25, with a dip in FY23, and was 7.3% in the second quarter of 2026.

Second-quarter 2026 gross revenue was $1,295 million, up $329 million. Payments-based revenue rose 24%, which the MD&A attributes to an $11 billion increase in volume and recent acquisitions. TFS revenue of $117 million came from Global Blue. Gross revenue less network fees rose 51%, primarily due to recent acquisitions, the increase in volume and higher subscription and other revenue.

The counter-case is how little of that growth reached profit. Income from operations rose only to $95 million from $83 million, as general and administrative expenses grew to $231 million from $131 million and depreciation and amortization rose with acquisitions. Interest expense rose to $65 million from $39 million because of debt issued for Global Blue, and interest income fell to $3 million from $19 million. Net income fell to $24 million from $41 million.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Total debt rose to $4.5B at the end of FY25 from $2.8B a year earlier, and net debt to $3.6B. Trailing net debt to EBITDA is 4.5x and interest coverage only 1.5x. That is the core risk in this stock: a fall in volume would leave little margin before leverage became a constraint.

The current ratio has fallen to 1.21 on a trailing basis from 1.66 at the end of FY25, which leaves a thinner short-term liquidity cushion. The 10-K's risk factors also refer to the company's Preferred Stock alongside its Class A common stock; the excerpt does not give its size or terms.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow was $400M in FY25, a 9.6% FCF margin, after 9.8% in FY24. Capital expenditure was $0.2B against operating cash flow of $0.6B. The MD&A shows why reinvestment is a real call on cash: the company depreciates equipment under lease to merchants and amortizes internally developed capitalized software. The trailing FCF yield is 10.8%.

That cash has competing claims. The higher interest expense described above is paid from it, and the pending acquisition requires an initial payment of approximately $143 million of cash. In FY25 the company repurchased $453M of stock while total debt rose sharply, so free cash flow has not yet been directed at deleveraging (see Management).

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $36.31 FOUR trades at 56.7x trailing earnings, 7.0x NTM earnings, ~5.9x FY27E earnings, 0.6x trailing sales and 7.6x trailing EV/EBITDA.

The gap between trailing and forward P/E reflects the basis. Consensus EPS of $5.21 for FY26E and $6.20 for FY27E sits far above FY25 diluted EPS of $1.08; the company reports non-GAAP EPS that excludes amortization of acquired intangibles and other items, so consensus is most likely on that basis. Even on that basis, a single-digit forward multiple implies little confidence in the estimates.

The Street is split: 12 Buy and 12 Hold, with a consensus target of $55.05, a median of $51.00 and a range of $40.00–$96.00. The low end of the Street range sits above today's price.

We have no peer multiples to compare against.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Volume growth continues, Global Blue synergies arrive and free cash flow is directed at debt. The shares re-rate to around the Street consensus target.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Shift4 delivers most of the consensus earnings path and starts to reduce leverage slowly. The shares settle between the lowest Street target of $40.00 and the median of $51.00.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Consumer spending and travel weaken, volume growth slows and interest costs absorb what free cash flow remains. Estimates fall and the shares break below the 52-week low.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries the most weight because it requires only most of the consensus path. We weight Bear above Bull: with interest coverage at 1.5x, a slowdown in volume would reach the equity quickly, while a re-rating needs deleveraging that free cash flow can deliver only gradually.

The result is a weighted fair value of $40.90, an expected upside of +12.6% and a bear-case downside of -28.4%. The upside clears our BUY threshold, but the reward per unit of bear-case risk does not, so we rate the shares HOLD.

Our $38–$48 target range brackets Base. It sits below the Street consensus target because we give more weight to the balance-sheet risk than the Street's average does.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Shift4 reports a single segment. The MD&A breaks gross revenue into payments-based revenue, TFS revenue and subscription and other revenue: in the second quarter of 2026 these were $1,073 million, $117 million and $105 million, respectively. Payments-based revenue is the core of the business, and TFS is the contribution from Global Blue.

moatFactors.name: Integrated software and payments
moatFactors.body: Shift4 offers point-of-sale software, business intelligence tools and payment processing together. In our view, a merchant using several of these products faces higher switching costs than one using a standalone processor.

moatFactors.name: Vertical focus
moatFactors.body: The company targets restaurants, hotels, stadiums, theme parks and luxury retailers, which the MD&A describes as the experience economy, and says it serves merchants from small local businesses to multinational enterprises. In our view, venues of this kind need point-of-sale, payments and, for international customers, currency services working together, which favors a provider that offers all of them over a generic processor; the filing does not quantify merchant retention.

moatFactors.name: Distribution network
moatFactors.body: Distribution through independent software vendors, value-added resellers and internal sales gives Shift4 broad reach. Those partners are paid residual commissions, so the relationships carry a cost.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. Integrated software and a vertical focus give Shift4 a position with its merchants, and volume growth, which reflects merchants processing more through the platform, supports that view even though much of the revenue growth was acquired. Competition in payments and TFS is intense (see Risks), so the advantage requires continued investment.

points: Consensus expects FY26E revenue of ~$5.1B, up 22%, below the second quarter's 34% growth. That slowdown is consistent with Global Blue, acquired in the third quarter of 2025, no longer adding to year-over-year comparisons from the second half of 2026.

Volume grew by $11 billion in the second quarter of 2026 compared with the second quarter of 2025. In our view, sustained volume growth is the best indicator of the core business, since it drives payments-based revenue.

In August 2026 Shift4 agreed to acquire an account-to-account payments company for an initial payment of approximately $143 million of cash, with contingent consideration of up to $173 million. It adds a payment method; our view on acquisitions at current leverage is in Management.
The shareholder letter's forward-looking statements refer to expansion of Shift4One in 15 countries by year end, which would broaden the international business.

management.leadership: Per the proxy statement dated April 2026, Taylor Lauber became Chief Executive Officer on June 5, 2025, and Christopher N. Cruz became Chief Financial Officer effective September 1, 2025. Founder Jared Isaacman resigned as CEO in June 2025 on his nomination as NASA Administrator, became Executive Chairman, and resigned that role upon his Senate confirmation; the Board appointed Mr. Lauber Chairman on December 17, 2025, and Mr. Isaacman was sworn in on December 18, 2025. The leadership team is therefore new, and its record on integration and deleveraging is still being established.
management.capitalAllocation: Shift4 has been acquisitive and has also repurchased stock: Global Blue in 2025, a pending account-to-account payments acquisition in 2026, and buybacks in FY25. The cost has been a large rise in debt. In our view, management's priority should now be deleveraging; further acquisitions or buybacks before interest coverage improves would keep us at HOLD.
management.governance: Per the proxy statement dated April 2026, five of the seven directors named, Sam Bakhshandehpour, Seth Dallaire, Karen Roter Davis, Jonathan Halkyard and Sarah Grover, are independent; Taylor Lauber and Nancy Disman are not. Shift4 ceased to be a controlled company on December 17, 2025, and may rely on exemptions from certain governance requirements until December 17, 2026. With an independent majority already in place, the practical effect of the exemption appears limited, and it ends within a few months. Approximately 91% of the CEO's 2025 total target compensation was in RSUs, which ties pay to the share price.
management.insiderOwnership:
Per the proxy, as of April 13, 2026 Jared Isaacman beneficially owned 28.66% of the Class A common stock, and all executive officers and directors as a group held 1.54%. Based on Schedule 13G/A filings from February to April 2026, BlackRock, Inc. held 8.79%, Durable Capital Partners LP 8.33%, Darlington Partners Capital Management, LP 7.02% and Wasatch Advisors LP 5.30%.

The Founder's block is far larger than current management's holdings, and he no longer has a role at the company. That gives one holder outside management significant influence over shareholder votes. The shareholder letter refers to future negotiations with the Founder without saying what they concern.

idiosyncratic: Leverage: the balance-sheet risk set out in Financials leaves little room if volume weakens. The shareholder letter's forward-looking statements list debt covenant compliance and debt service obligations among the uncertainties.
Integration: the 10-K warns that Shift4 may be unable to integrate Global Blue or realize the anticipated synergies, and that third parties may terminate or alter contracts.

Travel and spending: the MD&A says geopolitical and global trade tensions and military conflicts have caused travel disruptions and affected consumer spending. In our view, that matters for a business focused on hospitality and luxury retail.
Competition: the 10-K says some competitors are larger and may offer services at lower rates, and that TFS competitors, including app-based start-ups, are increasing in number.
risks.systemic: Shift4 earns payment revenue mainly as a percentage of the dollar volume it processes, so its results move with consumer spending at its merchants. A recession or a sustained travel slowdown would reduce volume across the business. With leverage already high, a downturn would also tighten the company's financial flexibility.

body: HOLD, target range $38–$48, based on the scenarios in Valuation.

We would move to BUY on evidence that free cash flow is reducing debt and interest coverage is improving. We would cut further if volume growth slows sharply, if consensus estimates start to fall, or if management prioritizes acquisitions over deleveraging.
